target.title: Allow single-account claude-swap cards
target.body:
## Summary

- add `claudeSwapShowSingleAccount`, an opt-in Claude provider setting that prefers claude-swap cards when exactly one account is available
- apply the same account-count precedence to the menu-bar app and `codexbar cards`, while retaining the existing 2+ account default
- preserve zero-account fallback and explicit CLI account/source overrides; document and test config compatibility on macOS and Linux

## Why

The claude-swap integration currently requires at least two rows before it replaces the ambient Claude presentation. Users who intentionally manage a single account through claude-swap therefore cannot use its valid quota snapshot when the ambient Claude account is unavailable or different.

Changing the existing threshold globally would risk replacing ambient presentation for users with stale or sentinel-only single rows. This keeps that behavior backward-compatible and makes the alternate precedence explicit.

Follow-up to #2188 and the claude-swap precedence introduced in #1909.

## Testing

- `swift build --product CodexBarCLI`
- [redacted live proof](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2280#issuecomment-5009539899): a real one-account setup renders `[claude-swap]`, the active account marker, and both quota windows
- synthetic `cswap --list --json` fixture renders `@ synthetic@example.com [active]` from a one-account config without invoking ambient Claude
- focused macOS/Linux tests added for disabled/enabled single-account behavior, sentinel rows, explicit bypass, and config Codable compatibility
- `make check` portable, documentation, locale, and SwiftFormat checks pass locally; local SwiftLint cannot load SourceKit under the Command Line Tools-only environment
- the Command Line Tools-only installation also lacks Swift `Testing` and the SwiftUI `PreviewsMacros` plugin, so focused tests and the app target are delegated to CI

target.body:
## Summary

Adds a ↻ trailing action button in the Cookie Source picker row for OpenCode Go and OpenCode providers in the settings pane.

## Behaviour

1. Clears the cached browser cookie from Keychain
2. Re-imports from all supported browsers (using the provider's browser import order)
3. Stores the fresh cookie
4. Triggers an immediate provider refresh

If re-import fails (e.g. running outside the signed app bundle), the cache is still cleared and the next auto-refresh will complete the import.

## Evidence

The same code path (`CookieHeaderCache.clear` → `importSession` → `store`) is exercised by the CLI command. See `docs/proof/cli-cookie-refresh-proof.md` in PR #2262 for the full test matrix.

Button UI verified via signed-app screenshot: located in the Cookie Source picker trailing area alongside the cached timestamp and source dropdown.

## Related

- Issue: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/issues/2260
- CLI PR: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2262

## Summary

- keep Command Code browser discovery on SweetCookieKit's full Chromium-family list, including Vivaldi

target.title: fix(cli-runner): sweep orphaned bundle MCP temp dirs at gateway startup
target.body:
Fixes #105641

## What Problem This Solves

Per-run bundled MCP temp configs (`os.tmpdir()/openclaw-cli-mcp-*/mcp.json`, containing the rendered loopback URL and resolved tokens) are only reclaimed by the in-memory `cleanup()` callback returned from `prepareModeSpecificBundleMcpConfig`. When the gateway process exits with runs in flight (restart, crash, SIGKILL), the callback dies with it and the directory leaks — credential-bearing files outlive the gateway generation that issued them, and restart-heavy deployments accumulate leaked dirs until reboot. 26 leaked dirs built up over 33 days on our production host, dates correlating 1:1 with restart activity (full field data in #105641).

## Approach

A gateway-startup post-ready sidecar (`sidecars.bundle-mcp-temp-sweep`, mirroring `sidecars.session-locks`) that removes orphaned dirs. Orphan detection is **liveness-based, not age-based**:

- Live CLI children carry the config path in their argv (`--mcp-config <dir>/mcp.json`, from `injectClaudeMcpConfigArgs`), so a dir is only removed when **no visible process references it**. Live-session dirs legitimately persist across turns — an age-only sweep would regress #73244.
- The config is rendered at prepare time, **before** the run enters the serialization queue, so a run waiting in the queue owns a config that no process argv references yet. To tell such a live-owned queued dir from a true orphan, the creating gateway's identity is encoded in the temp dir NAME, produced atomically by `mkdtemp`:

  ```
  openclaw-cli-mcp-<pid>-<boot8>-<startTicks>-<random>
  ```

  An argv-unreferenced owner-encoded dir is removed only once its owning gateway is **provably gone**: pid dead (`process.kill(pid, 0)`), host rebooted (`boot8` differs from the current Linux boot id), or the pid reused by a different process (owner's `/proc/<pid>/stat` start time differs). Off-Linux (no start verification) the sweep *over-protects* — it never deletes a live-owned config; that residual is the safe direction and is documented.
- **Legacy (pre-ownership) dirs without an encoded owner are never auto-removed.** Their owner cannot be proven, so during a rolling upgrade a concurrently-running older gateway could hold an unspawned queued run whose legacy config is aged and argv-unreferenced — deleting it would break that run. Legacy dirs are kept and surfaced via a startup `warn` with a count for explicit operator cleanup (stop the gateway, remove stale `openclaw-cli-mcp-*` by hand). Once a host runs an ownership-aware build every new dir is owner-encoded, so the legacy set only ever shrinks.
- The sweep **fails closed**: if the process scan yields nothing (restricted environment), everything is kept — keeping a leaked dir beats breaking a live run. A fresh argv re-scan runs immediately before removal so a child that spawns mid-sweep is kept.
- Process scan is async and cross-platform: `ps -axww` on POSIX, `/proc` walk fallback for minimal Linux containers without procps, PowerShell `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` on Windows, all with timeouts.
- The `mcp.json` write in `bundle-mcp.ts` is wrapped so a failed prepare rolls the dir back (closes a pre-existing leak).

### Why legacy dirs are never auto-removed (rolling-upgrade safety)

An earlier revision still age-swept unowned legacy dirs, which a review flagged as a P1: during a mixed-version rollout an older gateway can have a queued run older than any grace window with no child argv and no encoded owner, and the new gateway would remove a config that queued run still needs. Rather than gate legacy cleanup on a heuristic, this revision **stops auto-removing legacy dirs entirely** and routes their reclamation to explicit operator action (surfaced by the startup warn). This closes both the `merge-risk: compatibility` concern (a newly-upgraded gateway no longer changes the treatment of an older gateway's dirs) and the `merge-risk: availability` concern (no queued config is deleted before its child spawns) at the root.

This also removes the age-based spawn-grace window, which only ever protected legacy dirs — a **net simplification**. A live-owned queued dir is already kept by owner liveness, and a dead owner's config is reclaimable at any age, so no age check remains.

## Evidence

**Live reproduction of the leak on a production gateway (OpenClaw v2026.6.11, Ubuntu VPS), before this fix** — run in flight + `systemctl restart`:

```
novo temp dir: /tmp/openclaw-cli-mcp-V6tUnQ
>>> systemctl restart com run em voo...
LEAK REPRODUZIDO: /tmp/openclaw-cli-mcp-V6tUnQ sobreviveu ao restart do gateway
=== total dirs: 26
```

**Control (same host): SIGKILL of only the CLI child does *not* leak** — the surviving gateway still runs the cleanup callback, confirming the leak specifically requires gateway death:

```
novo temp dir detectado: /tmp/openclaw-cli-mcp-EB9IqM
SIGKILL enviado
dir foi limpo apesar do kill
```

**Focused tests.** `bundle-mcp-sweep.test.ts` covers, for the name-encoded scheme: gateway death with runs in flight, a live CLI child keeping its dir (#73244), a concurrent gateway's child, a live-owner queued dir kept, a dead-owner dir removed, a rebooted-owner dir removed, a **fresh** dead-owner reclaimed regardless of age, a **pid-reuse** dir removed (alive pid, mismatched start), an **unknown-start** dir kept (fail-closed), a **start-unverifiable** dir kept (off-Linux over-protect), **legacy dirs (aged, fresh, empty, unparseable) all kept** (rolling-upgrade safe), the legacy-retained operator **warn**, a child that **spawns between the argv scan and removal** kept, and non-matching entries / missing roots. `bundle-mcp.test.ts` asserts a config-write failure rolls the temp dir back. Lint (`pnpm lint`), `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `check:temp-path-guardrails` clean; `deadcode:exports` adds no export.

**After-fix exact-head real-behavior proof — real host process scanner (no mocks), Linux.** Ran the exported `sweepOrphanedBundleMcpTempDirs` (esbuild-bundled from the exact-head source — the real function, not a reimplementation) at head `c1b550b0` on a real Linux host (Node v22) with its real defaults: real `ps` scan, real `process.kill(pid, 0)` liveness, real boot id, real `/proc/<pid>/stat` start-time verification. Six temp dirs, none referenced by any live argv, owner encoded in each name. Redacted (no tokens, endpoints, host paths, or boot id):

```
== Setup (real defaults; no argv references any dir) ==
boot tag: <redacted-8hex>
live pid <L>: alive=true startTicks=299190727
dead pid <D>: alive=false
cases (owner encoded in dir name):
  openclaw-cli-mcp-<L>-<boot>-299190727-live       expect=keep    (live owner, start matches)
  openclaw-cli-mcp-<D>-<boot>-299190727-dead       expect=remove  (dead owner)
  openclaw-cli-mcp-<D>-<boot>-299190727-dead-fresh expect=remove  (dead owner, FRESH - no age check)
  openclaw-cli-mcp-<L>-<boot>-300178381-pidreuse   expect=remove  (pid alive but start MISMATCH - pid reused)
  openclaw-cli-mcp-<L>-<boot>-0-unknownstart       expect=keep    (unknown creation start 0, live pid - fail-closed)
  openclaw-cli-mcp-legacy-orphan                   expect=keep    (legacy old-format, aged - never auto-removed)

== sweepOrphanedBundleMcpTempDirs (real defaults) ==
removed: [ '...-dead', '...-dead-fresh', '...-pidreuse' ]
kept:    [ '...-live', '...-unknownstart', 'legacy-orphan' ]
warn:    bundle MCP temp sweep: retained 1 legacy (pre-ownership) temp dir(s); these are
         never auto-removed to stay rolling-upgrade safe. To reclaim pre-upgrade leaks,
         stop the gateway and remove stale openclaw-cli-mcp-* dirs by hand.

== Verification (on disk vs expectation) ==
  live owner, start matches                        expect=keep   got=keep   PASS
  dead owner                                       expect=remove got=remove PASS
  dead owner, FRESH (no age check)                 expect=remove got=remove PASS
  pid alive but start MISMATCH (pid reused)        expect=remove got=remove PASS
  unknown creation start (0), live pid             expect=keep   got=keep   PASS
  legacy old-format, aged - never auto-removed     expect=keep   got=keep   PASS

RESULT: PASS
```

The **legacy orphan is now kept** (rolling-upgrade safe) and the operator warn fires with its count; a **reused pid** (same pid, different real start time) is still reclaimed even though the pid is alive; an **unknown creation start** (`0`) with a live pid is kept (fail-closed — never compared). The concrete pid-reuse driver behind the availability risk is exercised on the final-head code with real `/proc` verification, and the rolling-upgrade driver behind the compatibility risk is closed by never auto-removing legacy dirs.

## Tests

`bundle-mcp-sweep.test.ts` (name-encoded scheme, owner liveness, legacy-never-removed, operator warn, argv-spawn race, fail-closed), `bundle-mcp.test.ts` (config-write rollback), `bundle-mcp.resume.test.ts` (resume-hash stability), `server-startup-post-attach.test.ts` (sweep sidecar mocked so the startup test doesn't touch the real tmpdir).
